relevance_note: One member of a 191-patient suspected-IEI CNV cohort, patient-191, carries a TNFAIP3 deletion with individual clinical features: 'A monoallelic loss of TNFAIP3 was caused by a heterozygous 59.9 kb deletion in patient-191'.
method_note: Read the whole Markdown by hand; no script transcribed any table (a short script only assembled the JSON). Scope: only patient-191 has a TNFAIP3 variant; the other 190 cohort members (other CNVs/SNVs or none) get no rows. Table 1 (CNVs and SNVs per patient) is present only as caption and notes, with no table body, and the supplement (Table S1, online supplementary discussion, Fig. S1/S2) is not in the file, so patient-191's sex, age, clinical diagnosis, genomic coordinates and any SNVs listed there could not be extracted. The text names no SNV for patient-191, so no other-gene variant rows. 'The carrier' in the discussion sentence listing rosacea, lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, pulmonary emphysema and chronic sinusitis refers to patient-191, named in the preceding sentence. Rosacea was mapped to the composite checklist item 'skin lesions (rash, folliculitis, erythema nodosum)' as observed (judgment call); chronic sinusitis was not counted as 'recurrent infections' and emphysema not as 'interstitial lung disease'. No disease label (e.g. A20 haploinsufficiency) is given to patient-191 personally; HA20 is mentioned only generally ('haploinsufficiency of A20 has been described to cause autoinflammatory disease'), so disease_label_as_stated is 'not reported'. The parental-testing statement is a study-wide limitation, not specific to patient-191; inheritance left 'not reported'. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is true because patient-005 (ICOS, out of scope) was previously reported in ref [23]; this does not concern the TNFAIP3 carrier. Cohort size 191 as stated; four samples were later excluded for poor data quality (patient-191 was not among them, since its CNV was validated). Contradictions noticed (out of scope persons only): patient-180's 22q11.2 deletion is '740.0 kb' in Results but '704 kb' in Discussion; the PIK3R1 variant is cited as 'MIM 171,833#0008' in Results and 'MIM 616,005#0008' in Discussion.
